target_customer: Tech company employees and founders with equity compensation who need wealth management
problem: Tech workers hold complicated equity, options and taxes that generic advisors handle poorly.
business_model: Fee-based wealth management and planning, from a few hundred dollars to tens of thousands of dollars a year depending on complexity

founders.name: Jordan Gonen
founders.background_notes: Search coverage calls the founders former software engineers who ran more than 1,300 consultations before launching; not confirmed on an opened page.

exit.acquirer: Merged with Alternativ Wealth (renamed Compound Planning)

competitors.name: Secfi
competitors.what: Funds startup employees' option exercises and taxes
competitors.funding_then: Raised 6 million dollars in 2019 per Fortune

technical_complexity.rationale: Software-enabled advisory is mostly standard web tooling around regulated human advice.

defensibility.rationale: RIA registration and client relationships create some stickiness but competitors could replicate the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; it merged with Alternativ Wealth in 2023.

market_need_then: A 2019 Schwab study cited in coverage found 76 percent of startup employees never exercise or sell pre-IPO options, pointing to need for specialized guidance.

branding.domain_note: Used withcompound.com, later redirected to compoundplanning.com after the merger.

identity.voice_and_tone: Gonen described the goal as the Apple of wealth management

rebrands.why: Merger; Alternativ Wealth rebranded as Compound Planning

branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage by TechCrunch and WealthManagement in Jan 2022 and an angel list with executives from Coinbase, Stripe, Brex and others.

brand_strength.rationale: Compounding metaphor fits finance and the name survived the merger, but no evidence of a distinctive identity.

outcome_analysis: Compound launched out of stealth in January 2022 with reported venture funding, serving tech employees with fee-based planning. In September 2023 it merged with Alternativ Wealth, whose CEO took over the combined Compound Planning while Gonen moved to a strategic role, so YC's Acquired label is a simplification of a merger. Terms were not disclosed and the reasons for combining are not stated in the sources opened.
notes: Funding conflict: WealthManagement (opened) says 37 million dollars in funding led by Greenoaks and Lachy Groom; a fintech.global headline and search summary say a 25 million dollar Series B. The round is recorded at 25 million with stage other because the stage label is not confirmed. Earlier rounds, if any, not found. Founder employers and education not found on opened pages. YC status Acquired differs from the merger; explained in outcome_analysis.
